title: Kubernetes vessel runtime: driver interface + Job-per-bead driver
description:
Make Kubernetes a first-class vessel runtime alongside Docker, removing the /var/run/docker.sock dependency in k8s mode.

1) Refactor internal/vessel behind a driver interface matching archon's vesselPool (Summon/List/Wait/Logs/Reap + Spec/Vessel); move the current Docker implementation to a docker driver. Existing labels (legion.managed, legion.bead.id, legion.vessel.name) become the shared contract, translated to k8s-safe label keys.
2) Add a kubernetes driver via k8s.io/client-go mapping one bead to one Job: backoffLimit 0 (Archon owns retries via beads), activeDeadlineSeconds from bead_timeout, TTL cleanup as janitor only — Archon remains sole authority to close/fail beads. Summon=create Job with env incl. LEGION_BEAD_ID + TRACEPARENT; List=Jobs by label selector; Wait=watch Job status, exit code from pod container status; Logs=pod logs; Reap=delete Job with propagation.
3) Config: runtime = docker|kubernetes selector plus [kubernetes] table (namespace, kubeconfig/in-cluster, resources, image pull secrets) in .legion/config.toml; docker stays default.
4) Secrets (GH_TOKEN etc.) come from a k8s Secret referenced in the Job spec, not plaintext env.
5) deploy/k8s manifests: Archon Deployment, ServiceAccount + Role/RoleBinding scoped to Jobs/Pods, Aspire Dashboard Deployment/Service.
6) Tests: client-go fakes mirroring existing vessel_test.go pattern; integration test behind a build tag needing a cluster (kind).
7) Docs: update architecture.md + new ADR 0007 recording Job-per-bead, label mapping, and reaper authority.

title: Replace 4-container obs stack with standalone Aspire Dashboard
description: Swap the docker-compose 'obs' profile (otel-collector, tempo, prometheus, grafana + deploy/obs configs) for a single mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspire-dashboard service that ingests OTLP directly. Expose 18888 (UI) and OTLP ingest; ensure the port/protocol matches internal/telemetry's OTLP HTTP exporter. Delete deploy/obs/. Update the compose header comment, README, and docs to point OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT at the dashboard. Document the trade-off: the dashboard is in-memory/ephemeral (dev-loop tool, no retention). Independent of the Kubernetes work and carries over unchanged to k8s later.
